h3.text: Separation: Keep personal expenses entirely separate from business ledger entries to maintain tax compliance.
h3.question: What must be kept entirely separate from business ledger entries to maintain tax compliance?

h3.text: Documentation: Always attach receipts or invoices to your ledger entries for audit trails.
h3.question: According to the documentation, what must be attached to ledger entries to create audit trails?

h3.text: Consistency: Record transactions daily to prevent errors and ensure accurate cash flow tracking.
h3.question: How often should transactions be recorded to prevent errors and ensure accurate cash flow tracking?

h3.text: Reconciliation: Compare your bank statements against your ledger at the end of every month to catch discrepancies.
h3.question: Why should you compare your bank statements against your ledger at the end of every month?

h3.text: Software Integration: While manual ledgers teach the logic, consider migrating to cloud accounting software once your transaction volume exceeds twenty entries per week to automate the balancing process.
h3.question: What transaction volume threshold triggers the recommendation to migrate to cloud accounting software according to the sentence?
h3.reference: once your transaction volume exceeds twenty entries per week

h3.text: Apply the debit and credit rules: Use the standard accounting equation (Assets = Liabilities + Equity). Debits increase assets and expenses; credits increase liabilities, equity, and revenue.
